resources.string: Ask for an app PIN (and optionally your fingerprint) when opening ShutterCtrl. An intervalometer series that\'s running keeps going.
ShutterCtrl talks only to your camera, on a USB cable or the local network: no cloud, no account, no analytics and no location access. Photos you download go straight to your library on this phone.

The PIN can\'t be recovered. ShutterCtrl will disconnect, reset its settings (your camera will ask to pair this phone again) and turn the app lock off. Photos you downloaded are in your library and aren\'t touched. If your phone has a screen lock, you\'ll confirm with it first.
Use your phone\'s screen lock to confirm it\'s you
Couldn\'t show the screen lock prompt
With a USB cable, or over the camera\'s own Wi-Fi or your home Wi-Fi. Nothing goes to Canon or the internet.
If Android asks, allow ShutterCtrl to use the camera.
If the camera asks, accept ShutterCtrl on the camera\'s screen.
No camera answered at %1$s. Check that the camera\'s Wi-Fi remote connection is waiting and that this phone is on the same Wi-Fi.
The camera refused the connection. Start the connection on the camera again and accept this phone.
The connection to the camera was lost.
That device isn\'t a Canon camera.
ShutterCtrl only connects to addresses on your local network (for example 192.168.x.x).
The USB cable was disconnected, so the session ended (a running intervalometer series was stopped). Plug the camera in again and tap it below to reconnect.
ShutterCtrl wasn\'t allowed to use the camera over USB. Tap the camera again and allow access.
Couldn\'t open the camera over USB. Close other apps that use it (for example a Files or photo import app), unplug the cable, plug it in again and retry.

Use a USB cable from the camera to the phone (a USB-C cable, or an OTG adapter). On many Canon cameras the USB port doesn\'t work for remote control while the camera\'s Wi-Fi is on, so turn Wi-Fi off on the camera first. The first time, Android asks whether ShutterCtrl may use the camera.
Plug in a Canon camera with a USB cable and turn it on. It shows up here.
Searching sends one discovery message on this Wi-Fi only.
Finds Canon cameras that announce themselves on the network
Many cameras don\'t announce themselves. Enter the address shown on the camera instead.
On the camera\'s own Wi-Fi, the camera is usually %1$s
The camera shows its IP address in its Wi-Fi settings. Only local addresses are accepted.
In the camera\'s wireless menu, start a Wi-Fi connection for remote control from a computer (EOS Utility) or a smartphone. Menus differ by model.
2. Put this phone on the same Wi-Fi
Join the camera\'s own network in Android\'s Wi-Fi settings, or let the camera join your home Wi-Fi. If Android says the network has no internet, choose to stay connected.
Search, use the access point address, or type the camera\'s IP address. The first time, accept ShutterCtrl on the camera.
The camera allows no change here in its current mode
The camera didn\'t accept that setting
The camera didn\'t take the picture. Check focus and the card.
See what the camera sees and change exposure
This camera doesn\'t offer remote live view
Live view uses the camera\'s battery faster. It stops when you leave this screen.
Send a firmware file you downloaded from Canon
Ends the remote session; the camera stays on
Keeps shooting with the screen off. A notification shows while a series runs, with Stop.
Shows while an intervalometer series is running, with Stop
Connect your camera on the Camera tab to see its card here.
Photos on the camera\'s card show up here.
Saved to Download/ShutterCtrl (this phone\'s media library doesn\'t know this RAW type)
Edit the JPEG or RAW file right away
Saved to Pictures/ShutterCtrl (RAW types this phone doesn\'t know go to Download/ShutterCtrl).
Install LumenCtrl to edit downloads straight from here.

Download the firmware file (.FIR) for your camera from Canon\'s website yourself, then pick it here. ShutterCtrl never goes online for this. The camera checks the file again and installs it only when you start the update on the camera.
How the file goes to the camera
Canon\'s own firmware transfer, as Camera Connect does it
Copied to the root of the card; then run Firmware update in the camera\'s menu
This camera accepts neither way from a phone. Copy the file to the card with a card reader.
From your downloads or any folder
The file\'s model id matches this camera.
This camera didn\'t report its model id, so ShutterCtrl can\'t compare it. I checked that this file is for my %1$s.
The file size doesn\'t look like Canon firmware.
The file name must be plain letters and digits, shorter than 32 characters (keep Canon\'s original name).
The camera didn\'t report its battery level. Charge it fully and reconnect.
The battery must be full. Charge it and reconnect.
This file is for another camera model.
This camera can\'t receive files from a phone.
%1$s is sent to the camera. Keep the camera on and close by, and don\'t leave ShutterCtrl until it\'s done. Then follow the instructions on the camera\'s screen to start the update.
%1$s is copied to the root of the camera\'s card. Keep the camera on until it\'s done. Then run Firmware update from the camera\'s menu.
Don\'t turn off the camera, open its card slot or battery door, unplug the USB cable or leave Wi-Fi range.
%1$s was sent. Follow the instructions on the camera\'s screen to start the firmware update. Don\'t turn the camera off while it updates.
%1$s is on the card. On the camera, open the menu, choose Firmware (Firmware update) and follow the steps. The camera checks the file before it installs it.
The firmware transfer stopped: %1$s. Nothing was installed. Reconnect and try again.
Your camera pairs with a random identity that ShutterCtrl made for this phone; it holds no name, account or serial number.
Your cameras will ask to pair this phone again
ShutterCtrl disconnects and makes a new identity. Each camera will ask you to accept this phone again.
Stopped after %1$d shots: the camera didn\'t accept a command.
Shots around the current exposure, for HDR or to be safe in tricky light. Autofocus runs on the first shot only. The camera\'s starting value is put back afterwards.
The camera\'s range ends before some steps; those shots use its nearest value.
The camera allows no other values right now

Set the lens switch to AF and focus on the nearest part you want sharp (Near and Far move the focus by one step). ShutterCtrl then takes a shot, moves the focus, and repeats, without autofocus. Merge the photos in a focus-stacking program afterwards. Leaving live view stops the stack.
The camera didn\'t move the focus. Is the lens set to AF?
Downloaded JPEG photos get where the phone was when they were taken
Location isn\'t allowed for ShutterCtrl any more. Allow it in Android\'s app settings, or turn this off.
Only approximate location is allowed, so positions can be off by a kilometre or more

Off until you turn it on. While it\'s on and ShutterCtrl is open, the phone notes its position (kept on this phone for 24 hours, never sent anywhere). A downloaded JPEG gets the position closest to its capture time, within 10 minutes, unless the camera already added one. RAW files are left as they are. Turning this off deletes the notes. The camera\'s clock should be right.
Location wasn\'t allowed, so geotagging stays off

The camera as a Bluetooth remote, the way Canon\'s BR-E1 remote works: Focus and Shoot without the camera\'s Wi-Fi. To pair, open the camera\'s wireless menu, choose pairing with a wireless remote, then tap Pair a camera here. Built from the open-source projects furble and eos-remote-web (used by others with the EOS M6, RP, R6 Mark II and 250D). Waking the camera and switching its Wi-Fi on over Bluetooth aren\'t included: no public source confirms how.
Not tried with an EOS R50 yet. Please report whether it works.
Focus and Shoot go over Bluetooth
The camera didn\'t take the command. Check that it\'s still connected.
The first time, Android may ask you to confirm pairing
Cameras waiting to pair with a remote appear here. Tap one to pair.
The camera must be on, with Bluetooth on
ShutterCtrl forgets it; remove it from Android\'s Bluetooth settings and the camera\'s menu too if you like
ShutterCtrl needs the Nearby devices permission for the Bluetooth remote
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and try again.
No camera found. Start pairing with a wireless remote on the camera and try again.
Couldn\'t connect to the camera. Check that it\'s on and close by.
This camera doesn\'t offer the Bluetooth remote
The camera didn\'t accept ShutterCtrl as a remote. Start pairing on the camera again.
Shown while the camera is on Bulb. The shutter stays open for the time you choose and closes again, also when you tap Stop or the time runs out.
Set the camera to movie mode first. Recording goes to the camera\'s card. Uses libgphoto2\'s movie record setting.
Records a movie to the card
The camera didn\'t start or stop the movie. Is it in movie mode?

%1$d files are deleted from the camera\'s card for good. Copies you downloaded to this phone stay.
%1$d couldn\'t be deleted (the camera refused, or the file is protected)
Download stopped at %1$d %%. Tap Download again to continue where it stopped.
